exposure: peak systolic blood pressure before discharge
patient systolic blood pressure per trimester
postpartum length of stay (<3 days or >=3 days)
discharge with or without blood pressure medications
discharge blood pressure thresholds for prescribing medication (>=130/80, >=140/90, >=150/100, >=160/110 mm Hg)
outcome: postpartum blood pressure spike (>=140/90 mm Hg while on antihypertensive medication or >=150/100 mm Hg if not on antihypertensive medication)
cohort: The study included 413 postpartum women who participated in remote blood pressure monitoring.
finding: The study identified three effective strategies to prevent outpatient postpartum blood pressure spikes: considering longer postpartum hospital stays or daily home monitoring for medium- and high-risk patients, prescribing antihypertensives at discharge for medium- and high-risk patients, and prescribing antihypertensive treatment if patients are discharged with a blood pressure of >=140/90 mm Hg.
